title: Saving a recording says it saved
goal: When you save a trimmed recording, nothing tells you it worked. A small save arrow on the floating controller quietly disappears and that is the whole confirmation. On a recording long enough for the save to take real seconds, the only sign anything is happening is a tiny spinner in the same spot, which is easy to miss, and the user described exactly that as "I click Save and it does nothing". Saving should say so, the way copying a recording already does.
notes:
Found while fixing trim-a-recording-save-it-send-it-the-whole-flow on 2026-09-19. The machinery already exists: AppCoordinator.toasts.presentProgress / dismissProgress and presentCopyToast are what the GIF copy path uses (AppCoordinator.swift around :305). VideoEditorState has no route to the coordinator today, which is why the save path has none of it; VideoEditorView.saveButton (around :474) is where the spinner lives now.

The close-confirmation case is the interesting one: the sheet dismisses, the save runs, and the window closes when it lands. For a long recording that is several seconds of a window sitting there apparently doing nothing before it vanishes.
acceptance: Saving a recording ends with a visible confirmation that names the recording, in the same toast family the copy and capture confirmations already use
While the save is running there is a progress indication that is readable from across the window, not a 28 point spinner on the floating controller
A save that takes under about half a second does not flash a progress indication at all, so short saves stay quiet
The confirmation appears for all three ways into a save: the controller button, Command S, and Save in the close confirmation

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) Walked it as a first-timer: trim an 8s clip, press the arrow, the arrow vanishes — that reads as 'the button went away', not 'it saved'. On a long recording the only sign is a 28pt spinner in the same spot. (2) Where should the confirmation live? The close-sheet path settles it: the window is GONE by the time that save lands, so an in-window notice cannot exist for one of the three ways in. The bottom-right toast stack is screen level and already means 'a thing about a recording finished' (the copy toasts). Toast it is. (3) Found by the review: a save with nothing to write must stay SILENT. save() on an up-to-date recording returns success without writing a byte; toasting there would both lie and let repeated Command S stack toasts. Only a commit that had a plan confirms. (4) A determinate bar with no real number is decoration: AVAssetExportSession.states(updateInterval:) exists on this SDK (probed, returns AsyncSequence<State, Never>), so the bar carries the encoder's own progress rather than sitting at 0%. (5) Shortest version: no new surface, no new window — the toast family that already exists, plus a delay so short saves stay quiet.

Built and verified. New walk saving-a-recording-says-so-walk: 43 steps, all green, with two real pictures of the app (the window after the save, and the toast itself). It proves all three ways in — the arrow on the controller, Command S, and Save in the close confirmation — each end with a named confirmation in the corner, and that the quick save flashed no progress at all. Three pieces of harness had to exist for that: expectToast (a walk could not see a toast before, because each one is its own panel), a Command S stand-in in PlaytestMenuStandIn (File > Save is dimmed for a walk's whole run, so the chord could only report the frozen menu bar back at itself), and a title on the toast panels so snapshot can photograph one. expectToast was watched running forced under a lock and read back the real line, so it is now on the lock-safe list with a test saying why.
